audience.text: Python developers who need to parse OneNote documents programmatically without requiring Microsoft OneNote installation or COM automation.

capabilities.text: Parse .one files from paths or binary streams into a DOM tree of Page, Outline, OutlineElement, RichText, Image, Table, and AttachedFile nodes.
capabilities.title: Parse OneNote documents

capabilities.text: Traverse the document tree using GetChildNodes for type-based search or DocumentVisitor for full traversal.
capabilities.title: Traverse document structure

capabilities.text: Extract text with per-run formatting including bold, italic, underline, hyperlinks, font name, size, and color via TextRun and TextStyle.
capabilities.title: Extract rich text with formatting

capabilities.text: Extract embedded images and attached files by accessing their bytes and file names for saving to disk.
capabilities.title: Extract images and attachments

capabilities.text: Inspect tables through Table, TableRow, TableCell, and TableColumn; and OneNote tags through NoteTag with labels and statuses.
capabilities.title: Inspect tables and tags

capabilities.text: Export pages to PDF using Document.Save with SaveFormat.Pdf and PdfSaveOptions for JPEG quality and image compression control.
capabilities.title: Export to PDF

capabilities.text: Inspect NumberList properties including format, number format, and restart behavior on OutlineElement nodes.
capabilities.title: Inspect numbered lists

capabilities.text: Handle library-specific exceptions including FileCorruptedException, IncorrectPasswordException, and UnsupportedFileFormatException.
capabilities.title: Handle exceptions

limitations.text: Writing back to .one files is not implemented — this library only reads OneNote files.
Password-protected documents are not supported — supplying a password raises IncorrectPasswordException.
SaveFormat currently declares only Pdf — Document.Save raises UnsupportedSaveFormatException for any other format.
License.SetLicense() and Metered.SetMeteredKey() are no-ops in this edition — no license is required to use this library.
DetectLayoutChanges() is a compatibility stub and performs no layout computation.
PDF export requires the optional reportlab dependency; it is not included by default.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic access to OneNote document content including pages, rich text, images, tables, attachments, tags, and numbered lists.
Supports exporting OneNote pages to PDF with configurable image compression and JPEG quality.
Provides a tree-based DOM traversal API using DocumentVisitor and GetChildNodes for structured document inspection.
Allows extraction of embedded images and attached files directly to disk without external dependencies.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Note FOSS for Python is a free, open-source Python library for reading Microsoft OneNote (.one) files and exporting pages to PDF.

uncertainties: The exact scope of 'OneNote Online' format support is not specified beyond FileFormat.OneNoteOnline being declared.
Whether PageHistory supports full revision history beyond the current page is unclear from available facts.
The behavior of Document.DetectLayoutChanges() in the commercial product versus this FOSS edition is not detailed beyond being a stub.

workflows.name: Load and inspect document
workflows.text: Load a .one file from path or binary stream using Document, then inspect its display name and node count.

workflows.name: Extract rich text with formatting
workflows.text: Traverse RichText nodes and inspect per-run formatting including hyperlinks, bold, italic, and font properties.

workflows.name: Extract embedded images
workflows.text: Iterate Image nodes, access their bytes and file names, and write them to disk.

workflows.name: Parse tables
workflows.text: Traverse Table, TableRow, and TableCell nodes to extract cell content as structured text.

workflows.name: Inspect OneNote tags
workflows.text: Access NoteTag objects attached to RichText nodes to read tag labels and statuses.

workflows.name: Export to PDF
workflows.text: Call Document.Save with SaveFormat.Pdf and optional PdfSaveOptions to generate PDF output.
